project 01

Echoes of
Resistance

Museum wayfinding kiosk

role
UX Designer, IA
course
UXP 434
audience
Students 8–18
stack
Figma · Three.js · Blender
year
2025

Overview

This kiosk focuses on the history of women's rights and triumphs, with landmarks and breakthroughs highlighted for each woman in individual timeline themed exhibits. Each category showcases not only their achievements, but the cultural and societal barriers they overcame, giving users a deeper understanding of the broader movements these women helped shape.

The home screen

The landing screen has one job. Get a visitor into a timeline before they lose interest. Three eras sit across the top as equal choices, so nobody has to guess where to start.

Below that, a carousel of previous sessions, a mission panel, and an alert desk with a headphone jack for anyone who needs audio support. Search sits last, as a fallback rather than the primary path.

Timeline format

By structuring the kiosk as a series of interactive exhibits, depicted as a timeline, users can explore key moments from early movements to modern day advocacy. They gain a more immersive appreciation of how these contributions continue to influence current conversations.

Each section carries a headline era, a spine of dates, and paired figure cards on either side, so a visitor can enter at any point without losing the thread.

The enclosure

The illuminated header sits high for gallery wide visibility while every interactive target is placed low, inside the ADA reach band, so the same enclosure works for an 8 year old, a standing adult, and a seated visitor without a separate kids mode.

Soft, rounded volumes suit the young audience. The screen is raked 15 degrees to shorten reach and cut overhead glare. The base carries a toe recess for wheelchair side approach, and the service panel is locked and out of public sightline.

Front elevation

Straight on, the hierarchy reads in one look. The illuminated beacon carries the identity above head height, the screen sits at 42 inches so it meets a standing adult and a seated visitor at roughly the same angle, and the tactile help button and headphone jack sit together at the lower left corner of the bezel.

In the round

From three quarters the 15 degree rake becomes obvious, along with the depth of the head assembly and the toe recess cut into the base for wheelchair side approach.

Outcome

A freestanding wayfinding totem that carries the Echoes of Resistance visual identity, delivered as an orthographic blueprint for fabrication review alongside a 3D model.

Drag the model to turn it. The proportions come straight off Sheet A-01.

Overview

The Simple Flourish is a marketing strategy and business support brand led by Sarah Del Castillo. Sarah works with women founders and service based business owners who want clearer marketing direction, stronger systems, and sustainable growth.

Her brand focuses on helping business owners move away from scattered marketing tasks and toward strategic decisions that support both the business and the person leading it.

The campaign theme

Business Without the Burnout was created to reflect Sarah's current business direction and the needs of her target audience. Many established women founders are not struggling because they lack effort. They are overwhelmed because they are trying to manage content, marketing, client work, planning, and business growth without a clear strategy or enough support.

This campaign speaks directly to that pain point by showing that growth does not have to come from doing more. It can come from clarity, structure, and strategic support.

What I delivered

I led the design track for a team engagement with a real client, from discovery through final handoff.

  • A 15 post social visual suite
  • Platform native LinkedIn and Instagram ad mockups
  • A landing page wireframe and full mockup
  • A content and distribution strategy
  • A client facing AI prompting toolkit so Sarah could keep producing on brand content after the engagement ended

Outcome

The campaign is designed for Instagram and LinkedIn because both platforms support Sarah's goals in different ways. Instagram allows polished visuals, educational graphics, carousel style content, and savable posts that connect emotionally with overwhelmed founders. LinkedIn supports a more professional and strategy focused tone, helping Sarah build credibility as a strategic partner.

The main goals are to increase brand awareness and build trust with Sarah's target audience, educate followers about the difference between random tactics and intentional strategy, and guide qualified leads toward a clear next step.

project 03

Animazed

Full stack e-commerce redesign

role
UX Designer
context
Website redesign
users
Adults 18–28
stack
Figma · Illustrator · InDesign
year
2025

Overview

A comprehensive full stack redesign for Animazed Online, an e-commerce platform dedicated to anime, manga, K-pop, and Danmei collectibles. The study assesses the entire user journey, emphasizing product design, UX tailored writing, and UX research.

Animazed operates a physical store in Raleigh, North Carolina, and is expanding its online reach. The target users are young adults aged 18 to 28 who are active online shoppers for fandom merchandise. This group emphasized a need for a more immersive browsing experience.

The primary goal was to evaluate the end to end user journey, focusing on:

  • Effectiveness of product categorization and navigation in facilitating purchases
  • Usability of specialized navigation tools such as filters
  • Streamlining the purchase journey for high stress, fast checkout scenarios
  • Aesthetic revision of the platform

Homepage

The original site used a fast cycling slideshow that cluttered the hero, plus a broken nav icon. The redesign introduces an immersive dark aesthetic with streamlined navigation and a cleaner visual hierarchy.

Browse and filtering

The original Shop All page used an overwhelming alphabetized list with no filtering logic, which meant excessive scrolling to reach anything. The redesign introduces dropdown filters organized by fandom, availability, and price.

Product page

The original product page ran on a stock template. Accurate, but it could have been selling anything. Nothing in the layout told a shopper they were in a fandom store.

The redesign adds a breadcrumb trail so the path back into browsing is always visible, moves the description into a Product Stats panel, and carries the store voice through the interface. Add to Cart becomes Claim Treasure. Related items become Based on your power level.

Cart and checkout

The original cart had no quantity safeguards, which allowed runaway orders. The revised checkout streamlines the flow with clear item summaries and corrected quantity controls.

It also surfaces the rewards balance at the moment of purchase, where a points total actually changes a decision, rather than burying it in an account page.

Community page

A broken sign up form obscured the community content entirely. The redesign surfaces relevant event data and uses a persuasive scroll driven layout to encourage sign ups naturally.

project 04

Cloud 9
Cherubs

Blind box collectible concept

role
Designer, 3D
scope
Character, packaging, collateral
stack
Procreate · Illustrator · Dimension · Photoshop
published
June 2025

Overview

Cloud 9 Cherubs is a blind box collectible concept I designed end to end, from character illustration through product and packaging design. The line centers on a cast of cloud dwelling cherubs built for the surprise and collect format that drives collectible brands like Sonny Angel and Pop Mart.

My goal was to make something genuinely covetable. Cute enough to display, distinct enough to want the full set, and polished enough to hold up on a real retail shelf. I owned every layer of it myself.

Sketch

I started with the emotional hook, because blind boxes live and die on anticipation. I wanted characters people would feel attached to before they ever opened the box.

I sketched the cherubs in Procreate, working through proportions, expressions, and the small collectible details that make each figure feel like its own thing.

Visual system

Once I locked the strongest concepts, I rebuilt them as clean vector art in Illustrator so they could scale cleanly across figures, stickers, and packaging without falling apart.

The cloud motif became the connective tissue for the whole line, giving me a flexible visual system I could carry from the brand sticker to the promo poster to the box art itself.

Product visualization

I rendered the figures and packaging in Adobe Dimension to pressure test how they would read as physical products, then composited everything in Photoshop for the retail ready mockups, sticker sheet, and poster.

Outcome

The final result reads as a cohesive collectible brand rather than a single illustration. Cloud 9 Cherubs pushed me past flat design into product design and brand identity, and it is one of the pieces I am proudest of for exactly that reason. Illustration, 3D visualization, packaging, and marketing collateral all speaking the same visual language.
